white-noise.q1: What is the difference between white, pink and brown noise?
white-noise.a1: White noise has equal energy at every frequency and sounds like hiss. Pink noise drops 3 dB per octave and sounds like steady rain. Brown noise drops 6 dB per octave and sounds like a low roar or distant surf. Green noise is centred on the middle of the range, around 500 Hz.
white-noise.q2: Which noise is best for sleep?
white-noise.a2: There is no single best one. Many people find pink or brown noise softer than white noise. Try each at a low volume for a few minutes and keep the one you notice least.
white-noise.q3: How does the sleep timer work?
white-noise.a3: Pick 15 minutes to 8 hours before pressing Play. The sound fades out over the last 30 seconds and stops. The fade is scheduled in the browser's audio engine, so it ends on time even in a background tab.
white-noise.a4: Keep the volume low, put the speaker well away from the cot and use the sleep timer. A 2014 study in Pediatrics found that some infant sound machines can pass 85 dB at full volume; hospital nurseries are kept under about 50 dB. You can check the level with the cv.cm decibel meter.
white-noise.q5: Does it need the internet or upload anything?
white-noise.a5: The noise is generated in your browser, so once the page has loaded it plays without any download. Nothing is uploaded.

decibel-meter.q1: How accurate is an online decibel meter?
decibel-meter.a1: It gives a useful estimate, often within a few dB after calibration, but it is not a certified sound level meter. Phone and laptop microphones differ and are less sensitive at very low and very high levels.
decibel-meter.a2: Decibels with A-weighting, which turns down low and very high frequencies the way human hearing does. Noise limits and hearing safety guidelines are usually given in dB(A). Choose Z (unweighted) to see the flat level.
decibel-meter.a3: Put a real sound level meter next to your device, play a steady sound, and change Calibration until both read the same. The offset is saved in this browser. Without a meter, compare with a known source such as a quiet room (about 30–40 dB).
decibel-meter.a4: Long exposure above 85 dB(A) can damage hearing. NIOSH recommends at most 8 hours at 85 dB(A), halving the time for every 3 dB more: 4 hours at 88, 1 hour at 94, 15 minutes at 100.
decibel-meter.q5: Is the sound recorded or uploaded?
decibel-meter.a5: No. The microphone signal is analysed in this tab and thrown away. Nothing is recorded, stored or uploaded.

voice-recorder.q1: How do I record my voice online?
voice-recorder.a1: Press Record and allow the microphone. Speak, press Pause if you need a break, then Stop recording. The take appears in the list, where you can play it and download it.
voice-recorder.a2: Chrome, Edge and Firefox record WebM (Opus), Safari records M4A (AAC). Download WAV converts the take to uncompressed audio that every editor and phone can open.
voice-recorder.a3: One take can be up to 120 minutes. Recordings are kept in this tab's memory, so very long takes on an old phone may run out of room.
voice-recorder.q4: Are my recordings uploaded or saved?
voice-recorder.a4: No. They stay in this tab until you download them. Closing or reloading the page deletes them, and the page asks first if a take has not been downloaded.
voice-recorder.q5: How do I get clearer sound?
voice-recorder.a5: Keep Voice cleanup on to reduce background noise and echo, hold the microphone 15–30 cm from your mouth, and record in a small soft room. Turn cleanup off for music, so the instrument is not treated as noise.

screen-recorder.q1: How do I record my screen online?
screen-recorder.a1: Press Start recording, choose the entire screen, a window or a browser tab, and press Share. Press Stop recording (or the browser's Stop sharing) when done, then Download.
screen-recorder.a2: Yes. With System or tab audio on, Chrome and Edge record the sound of a shared tab, and of the whole screen on Windows and ChromeOS. Firefox and Safari record the picture only. Turn on Microphone to add your voice; it is mixed with the other sound into one track.
screen-recorder.q3: Does it work on a phone?
screen-recorder.a3: No. Phone and tablet browsers do not let web pages capture the screen. Use the built-in screen recording: Control Center on iPhone and iPad, Quick Settings on Android.
screen-recorder.a4: Auto saves MP4 where the browser can write it (Safari, recent Chrome and Edge), otherwise WebM. MP4 plays almost everywhere; WebM plays in browsers, VLC and most editors.
screen-recorder.q5: Is there a watermark or upload?
screen-recorder.a5: No watermark and no upload. The video is recorded in this tab and only leaves it when you press Download. One recording can be up to 60 minutes.

triangle.q1: How do I solve a triangle?
triangle.a1: Enter three values, at least one of them a side: three sides (SSS), two sides and the angle between them (SAS), two angles and a side (ASA or AAS), or two sides and another angle (SSA). For a right triangle, two values are enough.
triangle.q2: How are the sides and angles labelled?
triangle.a2: Side a is opposite angle A, b opposite B and c opposite C. In a right triangle C is the right angle, so c is the hypotenuse.
triangle.a3: Two sides and an angle that is not between them (SSA) can fit two different triangles, one with an acute angle and one with an obtuse angle. The calculator shows both.
triangle.a4: Area = ½ × b × c × sin A, which gives the same result as Heron's formula. For a right triangle that is ½ × a × b.
triangle.a5: Angles are in degrees. Sides can be in any unit, as long as all of them use the same one; the area is in that unit squared.

triangle.title: Triangle calculator
triangle.privacyNote: Solved in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.
triangle.needThree: Enter any three values, at least one of them a side.
triangle.needRight: Enter any two values, at least one of them a side.
triangle.hint: Side a is opposite angle A, b opposite B, c opposite C. Use one unit for all sides.
triangle.twoSolutions: These values fit two triangles. Both are shown.
triangle.case_sss: Three sides (SSS): find each angle with the law of cosines.
triangle.case_sas: Two sides and the angle between them (SAS): the law of cosines gives the third side.
triangle.case_ssa: Two sides and an angle not between them (SSA): the law of sines gives the other angles.
triangle.case_asa: Two angles and the side between them (ASA): the law of sines gives the other sides.
triangle.case_aas: Two angles and a side (AAS): the law of sines gives the other sides.
triangle.case_right: Right triangle: Pythagoras and sine/cosine give the rest.
triangle.stepCosines: Third side: c² = a² + b² − 2ab · cos C (with the two known sides and the angle between them).
triangle.stepAmbiguous: sin B has two angles below 180°: one acute, one obtuse. Both leave room for C, so there are two triangles.
triangle.drawingLabel: Triangle with sides a = {a}, b = {b}, c = {c}
triangle.err_needThree: Enter at least three values (two for a right triangle).
triangle.err_needSide: Angles alone fix the shape but not the size: enter at least one side.
triangle.err_tooMany: Enter only three values; clear the others.
triangle.err_positive: Sides and angles must be numbers above 0.
triangle.err_angleRange: Each angle must be below 180° (below 90° besides the right angle).
triangle.err_angleSum: The angles add up to 180° or more, so they cannot form a triangle.
triangle.err_inequality: These sides cannot form a triangle: each side must be shorter than the other two together.
triangle.err_noTriangle: No triangle fits these values: the side opposite the angle is too short.
triangle.err_hypotenuse: The hypotenuse c must be the longest side.
triangle.err_rightTooMany: In a right triangle C is 90°: enter only two other values.

white-noise.lead: Play white, pink, brown or green noise for sleep or focus, with a sleep timer. Nothing is uploaded.
white-noise.s1b: Pick a Noise colour. The line under it says how each one sounds.
white-noise.s2b: Start with a low Volume. Choose a Sleep timer, or leave it Off to play until you stop it.
white-noise.s3b: Press Play. You can switch colour or volume while it plays; the timer fades it out at the end.

decibel-meter.lead: Measure how loud a room or machine is in dB(A) with your microphone. Nothing is recorded.
decibel-meter.s1b: Press Start and allow the microphone. Keep the device still and pointed at the sound.
decibel-meter.s2b: The big number is the current level. Min, Max and Average (Leq) build up while it measures.
decibel-meter.s3b: Next to a real sound level meter, change Calibration until both match. The offset is remembered.

voice-recorder.lead: Record your voice from the microphone and download it as WebM, M4A or WAV. Nothing is uploaded.
voice-recorder.s1b: Press Record and allow the microphone. Watch the level bar move as you speak.
voice-recorder.s2b: Use Pause and Resume for breaks, then press Stop recording. The take appears under Recordings.
voice-recorder.s3b: Play it back, then press Download for the original file or Download WAV for any editor.

screen-recorder.lead: Record your screen, a window or a browser tab with sound and save MP4 or WebM. No watermark, nothing uploaded.
screen-recorder.s1b: Choose Format and Quality. Tick System or tab audio and Microphone as needed.
screen-recorder.s2b: Press Start recording, pick the entire screen, a window or a tab, and press Share.
screen-recorder.s3b: Press Stop recording when done, check the video, then press Download.

triangle.lead: Solve any triangle from three values, or a right triangle from two. Nothing is uploaded.
triangle.s1b: Tick Right triangle if C is 90°. Side a is opposite angle A, and so on.
triangle.s2b: Type three values (two for a right triangle), at least one of them a side.
triangle.s3b: Every side, angle, area, perimeter and height appears with a drawing and the working. Copy result copies it.
